name: New Orleans
tagline: 25-cent martinis at a 19th-century classic, and beignets worth the line every time.

Commander's Palace.description: Creole and Cajun cuisine since the 19th century, winner of seven James Beard awards. The 25-cent martini lunch is a local ritual. Critic Ian McNulty (Times-Picayune / NOLA.com) wrote: "Nobody makes fine dining more fun than Commander's."

Café du Monde.description: Beignets and chicory coffee at the French Market since the 19th century, with a constant line and zero pretension.

Galatoire's.description: French Creole cuisine on Bourbon Street since 1905, now run by the fourth generation of the Galatoire family.

Dooky Chase's Restaurant.description: Creole cooking since 1941 and a historic meeting point of the Civil Rights Movement, with Martin Luther King Jr. among its visitors.

Domilise's Po-Boy & Bar.description: A no-frills family-run po-boy shop since 1918. Anthony Bourdain ordered the off-menu special (fried shrimp, Swiss cheese, and roast beef gravy) on "No Reservations" (2008) and said he'd have a serious problem if he lived nearby. Holds a Michelin Bib Gourmand distinction.

Antoine's Restaurant.description: America's oldest continuously family-run restaurant, opened in 1840. Birthplace of oysters Rockefeller, now run by the fifth generation of the Alciatore family.

Arnaud's.description: A French Creole institution in the French Quarter since 1918, with a warren of historic dining rooms and over a century of classic New Orleans cooking.

Tujague's.description: New Orleans' second-oldest restaurant, opened in 1856 next to the French Market. Its bar invented the Grasshopper cocktail in 1918.

Brennan's.description: A French Quarter brunch institution since 1946, birthplace of Bananas Foster, invented here in 1951.

Jacques-Imo's Cafe.description: An unpretentious Uptown spot famous for its alligator sausage cheesecake and fried chicken, with a constant line and a loud, convivial vibe.

Mandina's Restaurant.description: An iconic pink building in Mid-City that went from Italian grocery to family restaurant in 1932, serving gumbo and Creole-Italian cooking largely unchanged for generations.

Cochon.description: Pork-driven Cajun cooking from chefs Donald Link and Stephen Stryjewski, both James Beard Award winners for Best Chef: South (2007 and 2011).

Bayona.description: Chef Susan Spicer's eclectic cooking in a 200-year-old cottage in the French Quarter; Spicer won the James Beard Award for Best Chef: Southeast in 1993.

Restaurant August.description: Chef John Besh's French-Creole fine dining in a 19th-century warehouse, which earned him the James Beard Award for Best Chef in 2006.

Shaya.description: Chef Alon Shaya's modern Israeli cooking, named America's Best New Restaurant at the 2016 James Beard Awards.

Willie Mae's Scotch House.description: A fried chicken house in Tremé since 1957, named an America's Classic by the James Beard Foundation in 2005 and now run by Willie Mae Seaton's great-granddaughter.

Parkway Bakery & Tavern.description: A Mid-City po-boy shop since 1911, where the Obama family made an unannounced stop for shrimp po-boys and turkey-and-alligator gumbo in 2010.

Mother's Restaurant.description: A po-boy shop in the Central Business District since 1938, famous for the Ferdi Special (roast beef and ham) and its debris gravy.

Central Grocery.description: A 1906 Italian grocery that invented the muffuletta, the cold-cut, cheese and olive-salad sandwich that came to define a New Orleans lunch.

Verti Marte.description: A 24-hour deli in the French Quarter, famous for the 'All That Jazz' sandwich (turkey, ham, shrimp and 'wow sauce'), cash only, no seats.

Turkey and the Wolf.description: A casual sandwich shop in the Lower Garden District, named America's Best New Restaurant by Bon Appétit in 2017, from chef Mason Hereford.

Li'l Dizzy's Cafe.description: Creole soul food from the Baquet family in Tremé, with fried chicken and gumbo served the same way for generations.

Casamento's Restaurant.description: Oysters and its famous oyster loaf on special pan bread since 1919, in an Italian-tiled dining room that has barely changed in a century.

Acme Oyster House.description: A French Quarter oyster house since 1910 that shucks more than a million oysters a year; a must-stop even with a line out the door.

Drago's Seafood Restaurant.description: Birthplace of charbroiled oysters, invented here in 1993 by Tommy Cvitanovich with garlic, butter and Parmesan cheese.

GW Fins.description: A French Quarter seafood restaurant praised by the Times-Picayune, Food & Wine and Esquire, a pioneer in dry-aging fish the way steakhouses age beef.

Pêche Seafood Grill.description: A wood-fire seafood grill from chefs Donald Link, Stephen Stryjewski and Ryan Prewitt, named America's Best New Restaurant at the 2014 James Beard Awards.

Angelo Brocato's.description: A Sicilian ice cream and pastry shop in the heart of Mid-City since 1905, still serving the lemon granita and cannoli the founder made from day one.

Hansen's Sno-Bliz.description: A snowball stand since 1939 using the original ice-shaving machine invented by Ernest Hansen; won the James Beard Foundation's America's Classic award in 2014.

District Donuts Sliders Brew.description: Rotating-flavor donuts and sliders in the Lower Garden District, including a crackly-topped cinnamon roll that goes toe-to-toe with the country's famous chains.

Napoleon House.description: A historic bar inside an 1797 building, the first place in America to serve a Pimm's Cup and still the world's top seller of the drink.

Carousel Bar.description: New Orleans' only revolving bar, installed in 1949 inside the Hotel Monteleone, a National Literary Landmark once frequented by Faulkner, Tennessee Williams and Truman Capote.

Pat O'Brien's.description: The French Quarter bar where the Hurricane cocktail was born in the 1940s, when wartime liquor shortages forced bartenders to invent something rum-heavy.

Cure.description: A craft cocktail bar on Freret Street that kick-started New Orleans' modern cocktail scene and won the James Beard Award for Outstanding Bar Program in 2018.

Pizza Delicious.description: A New York-style pizzeria in Bywater, ranked among the country's best pizzerias by the 50 Top Pizza and Pizza Slice USA lists.

Crescent City Steak House.description: New Orleans' oldest family-owned steakhouse, opened in 1934, which invented the local style of cooking steak sizzling in butter.

PJ's Coffee.description: A coffee chain born in New Orleans in 1978, roasting beans locally and still feeling like a neighborhood spot despite its growth.
